lines.text: Why does a dead battery bounce and a brand new one just thuds?
He checks them with a meter and the bouncy ones read just 1.2 volts.
Because inside a fresh AA the zinc is a soft gel that soaks up the hit.
beats: ai:cutaway of a fresh AA battery showing soft grey gel inside
ai:a soft grey gel cube absorbing a falling steel ball in slow motion

lines.text: And as the battery drains that zinc turns into zinc oxide which is stiff and springy so the dead one bounces.
beats: ai:white zinc oxide crystals forming inside a battery macro
ai:a springy rubber ball bouncing high off concrete in slow motion

lines.text: Then he drains every brand on a machine to see which one really lasts.
The dollar store battery costs thirteen cents and dies in 26 minutes.
And the Duracell lasts 381 minutes which is almost fifteen times longer.
The Energizer lithium lasts 723 minutes which is almost double the Duracell but it costs a dollar fifty each.
But the real winner is the one nobody expected.
Amazon Basics gives you 32 milliamp hours for every single penny which beats every brand he tested.
beats: ai:a single shiny copper penny standing next to an AA battery macro

lines.text: So the best battery and the best deal are two completely different things.
And now you know why the dead one bounces.
